newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain, Algeria to coordinate terrorism fight.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain, Algeria to coordinate terrorism fight.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual said on Wednesday that his country and Bahrain would join forces to combat terrorism.

"There will be coordination between Bahrain and Algeria to wipe out terrorism from the Arab world," the Gulf News Agency quoted Zeroual as saying after talks with Bahraini officials on a visit to the Gulf Arab state.
Zeroual said the Arab world needs to mobilise to fight terrorism.
He said Algeria felt the impact of "this dangerous phenomenon (terrorism) and its effects on other Arab and Islamic countries."
At least 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
In Bahrain, about 27 people have been killed, including three policemen and seven Bangladeshis, since anti-government protests broke out in December 1994 by members of the Shi'ite Moslem community.
Zeroual said that Bahrain and Algeria would set up a joint committee to promote cooperation in economic, trade, political and investment fields.
He arrived in Bahrain on Tuesday night on the first visit by an Algerian leader to the island state.
Zeroual will travel to China on Thursday for a five-day visit and then head to Vietnam. He is due to visit Qatar on his way back to Algeria.
